learningObjective: Distinguish the kinds of fusion XLA performs (loop, input, output) and their motivations.
stem: Which statements about XLA's operator fusion are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: XLA distinguishes multiple fusion kinds (e.g., 'loop' fusion, 'input' fusion, 'output' fusion) chosen based on producer/consumer memory-access patterns, so that fused kernels avoid materializing intermediate tensors when the access pattern is compatible.

Elementwise ops chained with reductions can be output-fused into the reduction kernel so the elementwise stage runs inside the reduction's inner loop and no intermediate tensor is written to global memory.
XLA always fuses any two adjacent ops in the HLO graph; fusion has no cost model and no boundaries, so producer/consumer pairs are unconditionally combined into one kernel.
Fusion in XLA operates by cloning the producer's HLO source into the consumer's IR file at compile time; there is no compiler-side representation of a fused kernel, only a copy at the string level.

explanation: XLA's fusion pass has multiple named kinds (loop, input, output, custom) and a heuristic/cost-model-driven decision procedure. Loop fusion combines elementwise producer/consumer chains; input fusion pulls producer computation into a consumer's input load; output fusion combines an elementwise epilogue into a reduction or dot's output. Fusion is bounded — not every adjacent pair is fused (register pressure, shape mismatch, opaque calls, etc. all create boundaries). Fusion is a proper IR transformation: XLA represents a fused kernel as an HLO `fusion` op with a nested computation, not as source cloning.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: multiple fusion kinds with memory-access rationale.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: output/epilogue fusion is a canonical XLA optimization.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: fusion is bounded by cost heuristics.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: fusion is an IR-level `fusion` op with a nested computation, not source cloning.

assumptions: XLA fusion pass as documented; naming may evolve but the taxonomy is stable.
nonImplications: Does not imply that maximally fused code is always fastest; register/SMEM pressure creates trade-offs.
Does not imply fusion is only for GPU; XLA does CPU fusion too.

distractorRationales.D: Confuses IR fusion op with textual duplication.
